name: vcm-drive-impedance
description: V_cm drive-impedance / decoupling sensitivity (issue #260). The sim/adc-inl-dnl/ deck's analyses / measure / checks blocks, copied byte-for-byte so every sweep point is point-for-point comparable with that experiment's own records, run against the SAME generated converter with its ideal V_cm source replaced by a real R || L (source impedance) + C_dec (decoupling) network -- the V_cm analogue of the V_REF network already in this same deck (DR-0002). Each recorded run overrides the netlist with `--netlist <variant>` + `--netlist-provenance 'schematic (...)'`; the variant decks are emitted by sim/vcm-drive-impedance/gen_vcm_variant.py, which patches only the one line the ideal V_cm source sits on and asserts a hit count so drift cannot silently patch nothing. The Z_vcm = 0 (ideal) point is not a variant at all -- it is the UNMODIFIED checked-in sim/adc-inl-dnl/testbench/tb_adc_inl_dnl.spice, which is exactly the assumption issue #260 exists to test.
claim: spec/decision-records/DR-0026-vcm-drive-source.md's derived V_cm drive-impedance / decoupling budget (Z_vcm,max <= 220 ohm, C_dec,min >= 40 nF). NOT the ratified README.md#target-specification rows directly: this experiment measures whether the SAME converter-level metrics sim/adc-inl-dnl/ reports (its own gain_err_lsb / inl_t*_lsb, which that deck's own checks already state are NOT the ratified Gain error, systematic row -- see its gain_err_lsb check description) move when the ideal V_cm source is replaced by a real network at and beyond the derived budget. A movement here is evidence the budget is load-bearing for the mechanism DR-0026 derives, not a pass/fail against a spec row.

code_t1.description: END-TO-END LIVENESS CHECK at transition 1: the converter must actually produce a code near 1 for an input 0.25 LSB above that transition's ideal voltage -- i.e. the whole chain (acquire, ten trials, decode) ran and tracked the input. The tolerance is +/-45 LSB rather than +/-0.5 because the converter carries a MEASURED converter-level gain error of ~31 LSB full-scale, dominated by top-plate parasitic loading of the array by the comparator's own input capacitance (DR-0011 samples on the top plate and the comparator inputs ARE that node). That is a gain term, reported by gain_err_lsb and analysed in spec/testbench-suite-memo.md; the LINEARITY claim is inl_t1_lsb below, which is evaluated after gain and offset are removed and is NOT relaxed here.

decerr_t1_lsb.description: Worst input-referred error over ALL TEN decisions of the conversion at transition 1, not just the deciding one: |err| gated to the ten comparator-strobe windows, so it reports the error each decision was actually taken with and ignores the settling excursion in between, which nobody samples. Bounds the early-trial errors that a plain-binary SAR with no redundancy (DR-0009) cannot recover from. The bound is the same ~31 LSB gain term the code check above absorbs, with margin -- an early trial's residue carries the full gain error, so this cannot be tighter than it without restating the gain claim.

The bound is the same ~31 LSB gain term the code check above absorbs, with margin -- an early trial's residue carries the full gain error, so this cannot be tighter than it without restating the gain claim.

gain_err_lsb.description: Converter-level systematic gain error, extrapolated from the two endpoint transitions to full scale. NOT the ratified Gain error, systematic row's claim -- that row is scoped by DR-0012/DR-0013 to the sampling switch's charge injection, and DR-0014 invalidated the 0.421 LSB evidence behind it by removing the switch it was measured on. Under the SUPERSEDED top-plate sampling phase this measurement was a different, larger term the ratified table has no row for at all -- top-plate parasitic loading, C_par/(C_arr + C_par), measured end-to-end at ~3 % of full scale and independently by sim/top-plate-cpar/ -- and that is what DR-0014 exists to remove. Under THIS topology both the sampled input and every DAC step sit over the same C_arr + C_par, so the derivation says the term should cancel to the accuracy the two sides match, and this number becomes the direct test of the record rather than a report of a known defect. It is a DERIVATION until #61 re-runs this deck: no measurement on this topology exists. The +/-60 LSB window is inherited unchanged from the superseded run and is deliberately not tightened here, because tightening it would assert the outcome of that run in advance. See spec/testbench-suite-memo.md and DR-0014.

vref_droop_mv.description: Peak-to-peak movement of the V_REF node across the whole measured window, through DR-0002's ratified >= 40 nF / <= 240 ohm envelope. Reported because it is the one error mechanism in this deck that is a property of the USER's network rather than of the block. The process-axis floor is the corner-sensitivity assertion this deck carries: the charge the array demands per conversion is set by the MiM sections and the switch R_on, so a sabotaged corner sweep (sim/harness/README.md) collapses it.

evidence.linearity_method: reduced-code-set-major-carry -- 18 probed transitions (1, 2, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257, 384, 511, 512, 513, 640, 767, 768, 769, 896, 1022, 1023) targeted at DR-0011's OWN array: the weight-256 sub-array MSB carry at 255->256 and 767->768 (the largest charge-division ratio this array forms, and independently the slowest-settling trial per sim/cdac-bit-settling/ and the analytically worst code per sim/mc-cdac-mismatch/), the free-MSB transition at 511->512 (where all nine switched weights change state but the deciding bit forms no ratio at all, because the free MSB is decided before any array switching -- a property DR-0014 keeps), weight-128 carries spanning the range, and both endpoints as the endpoint-fit anchors. Each transition is read at the trial that resolves it, from a full transistor-level conversion, against an ideal shadow DAC driven by the controller's own switch-driver outputs -- one conversion per transition, not a fine input search. NOT assumed binary-weighted-with-a-mid-scale-carry: see the netlist header.
notes: This is a SENSITIVITY experiment, not a re-verification of the ratified INL/DNL or Gain error rows: it reuses sim/adc-inl-dnl/'s own analyses verbatim so its gain_err_lsb / inl_t*_lsb numbers are point-for-point comparable with that experiment's records, but the corner grid here is deliberately reduced (see Corner matrix run / subset-reason at run time) to the cap-relevant `cdac` process axis at nominal temperature and supply only -- the axis this mechanism's charge/impedance interaction rides on (C_u via the mim_ff/mim_ss corners), per sim/harness/README.md's own guidance that a MOS-only sweep leaves both capacitor families typical.

V_cm is modelled exactly the way this SAME deck already models V_REF (DR-0002): an ideal source behind an R || L network (DC-accurate, resistive at the 16 MHz bit-clock band) feeding a decoupling capacitor. The Z_vcm = 0 point is the UNMODIFIED checked-in deck -- every existing sim/adc-inl-dnl/, sim/adc-enob-fft/ and sim/adc-power/ record already IS this experiment's ideal-source data point.

The R || L network's inductor is tuned to put the R-L corner at the 16 MHz bit clock (matching the V_REF network's own convention), which makes the network a genuine, if lightly damped, resonant tank with C_dec -- NOT a simple single-pole RC. The measured degradation vs. Z_vcm is real but NOT monotonic across the two non-ideal points tested here (see the record): a real external decoupling network's parasitic inductance is unspecified in practice, so the exact per-code sign and magnitude reported here is sensitive to that modelling choice, not a universal statement about any 220 ohm / 40 nF network. What is robust across both non-ideal points is that neither is near zero.

This experiment does not re-run ENOB/SFDR: those rows already fail for unrelated, tracked reasons at the ratified design (DR-0025, sim/adc-enob-fft/), which would make a V_cm-attributable delta hard to isolate from the existing acquisition-RC/top-plate-parasitic regression. gain_err_lsb and the endpoint-adjacent inl_t*_lsb values are the cleaner, still-passing metrics this record uses instead.
